items.text: Starting 15 March, the v1 endpoints of the Meridian Ledger API will be retired. Clients still calling /v1/transactions should migrate to /v2/transactions before that date; the v2 response wraps each record in a data envelope and paginates with cursor tokens instead of page numbers. We recommend you ignore the old rate limits during the transition window and test against both versions in sandbox. If your integration uses the legacy XML export, contact integrations@meridianledger.example immediately so we can schedule a guided cutover. Full migration notes and sample payloads are in the developer portal.

The finance team has asked everyone to submit Q1 expense claims through Concur by Friday. Receipts are required for anything over £25, and please remember that mileage claims need a map screenshot attached. If a claim is rejected, don't resubmit it — reply to the rejection email with the corrected figures and we'll push it through manually. Jordan has set up an automated tool that flags duplicates before submission, so most of you will get a warning within an hour if two people claim the same taxi. Any questions, ping accounts-payable@northwind-ops.example.

Data migration status — Week 6

We've moved roughly 1.4 million customer records from the legacy Billing platform into the new CRM so far, which puts us about a week behind the original plan. The bottleneck has been address normalisation: the old system stored postal addresses as free text, and roughly 9% of rows fail the new validation rules. Priya's team is working through the flagged records in batches, prioritising accounts with open invoices.

The second issue is duplicates. Because the legacy database allowed the same company to be entered multiple times with slightly different names, we're seeing a fair number of merges that need a human decision. Please do not approve merge suggestions blindly — the deduplication review queue is there for a reason, and a wrong merge is painful to unwind. Anyone with access to the staging environment can help clear the queue; instructions are on the wiki under Data Ops / Dedupe.

One reassurance for anyone worried about the timeline: nothing is being deleted from the old system until we've had two clean reconciliation cycles, and the audit trail is intact throughout. We'll publish a revised schedule next Tuesday. If you spot records that look corrupted or out of order, raise a ticket with the data migrations label rather than fixing them by hand.

We used a chatbot to draft the first pass of the deprecation notice, then rewrote most of it by hand. The final version keeps the same takeaway as before: teams relying on the v1 webhook callbacks must switch to signed deliveries before the shutdown, or their listeners will silently stop receiving events. For testing, ignore the unsigned samples in the old docs — they're out of date and were the cause of most of last month's support tickets. The engineering blog has an updated walkthrough with curl examples.
Expense tip: if your receipt is in a foreign currency, the card statement amount is what we reimburse, not whatever the conversion widget gives you — ignore the second figure in the app.

Following last night's migration run, you may notice that some cost centres in your expense history now show the new six-digit codes. Nothing has been lost — the old codes are still searchable, and approvals already in progress will complete under the old numbering. Managers should disregard the automated email about "orphaned" claims; those are simply records waiting for the second mapping pass to finish. We expect everything to reconcile by Wednesday lunchtime.

The API deprecation notice went out to 3,200 developer accounts yesterday. Within hours we'd had more than a hundred replies, mostly from people asking for an extension because their release cycles don't line up with our March deadline. We're granting a blanket 60-day grace period: the v1 endpoints will keep responding until mid-May, though we'll log every call so we can chase the stragglers. Please don't ignore the warnings in the response headers during that period — they'll tell you exactly which endpoints are still being hit and by which key.

Our support chatbot has been updated to answer the most common migration questions, including how to map legacy billing codes to the new chart of accounts. It's good at the basics but it does occasionally invent a field name, so treat its answers as a starting point and check the mapping spreadsheet for anything that touches money. If the bot can't help, the migration desk is staffed 9 to 5, Monday to Thursday, on extension 4412.

A note on expense claims while we finish the platform migration

For the next few weeks, all expense claims must go through the old FinancePortal rather than the new app. The new app's approval workflow still points at the legacy cost centres, and approvals submitted there after the cutover won't reach your manager. This affects everyone in the UK and Ireland entities; the German team moved over last month and can continue as normal.

To submit, log in with your existing SSO credentials and ignore the banner about the retirement date — it's stale and we haven't been able to remove it yet. Claims under £50 with a photograph of the receipt can go in without pre-approval, as before. Anything above that needs a cost centre and a project code, and the project code dropdown will be empty for a small number of people whose profiles weren't migrated in the first batch; if that's you, email finance-systems@aldermay.example with your employee number and we'll fix the profile within a day.

Finally, if you already submitted a claim through the new app between the 3rd and the 7th, don't worry — those have been recovered and will be processed manually. You don't need to resubmit them, and doing so will create duplicates that take longer to clear. The help pages will be updated once the workflow is repointed, which we expect in the week of the 24th.
Note for reviewers: the migration runbook now says to ignore step 4 (the manual checksum) because it's handled automatically by the verification job.
